result.title: CAST: Calibrating Correspondences for Training-Free Biomedical In-Context Segmentation
result.summary: Biomedical image segmentation must keep up with new anatomical structures, subjects, imaging modalities, and acquisition protocols, yet dense expert annotations are scarce and models trained on one cohort often struggle to transfer. In-context segmentation (ICS) offers a way out: a new structure is specified by a few annotated exemplars at inference time. However, reliable correspondence remains challenging in biomedical images, where adjacent structures often share similar appearances, and variations across subjects and imaging conditions further obscure their distinctions. We introduce CAST, a training-free framework built on a frozen DINOv3 backbone to calibrate fine-grained correspondences. Its stability test improves feature reliability at both global and patch-specific levels, while its coherence test assesses whether candidate correspondences are supported by consistent local structural context. Together, these tests enable more reliable correspondence across diverse anatomical structures and imaging conditions. Across eight biomedical benchmarks spanning 2D and 3D segmentation, cross-subject, and cross-modality transfer, CAST outperforms the strongest overall baseline by 12.34 percentage points in Dice and ranks first across all six volumetric settings. The versatility of CAST further opens up opportunities for challenging biomedical applications, including 2D-to-3D segmentation and atlas label transfer.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 CAST：一个基于冻结 DINOv3 的无训练生物医学 in-context 分割框架。论文用稳定性测试在全局与 patch 级校准特征可靠性，并用一致性测试判断候选对应是否得到局部结构上下文支持，以改善跨结构、跨受试者与跨模态的细粒度对应；在八个生物医学基准上报告 Dice 提升。
AI.relevance_reason: 该文本身是无需训练的分割对应方法，但其中「稳定性筛选特征、局部上下文一致性校验对应」的线索，可能可供核查 LVR 中视觉证据筛选与 latent 相似度可靠性判断的做法；尚未涉及推理期状态或答案使用 latent 内容。
